events.description: State Department Rewards for Justice offered $10 million for information on Muhammad Kawtharani.
actors: US State Department Rewards for Justice

events.description: US Treasury designated Kawtharani as a global terrorist.
US airstrike killed Qasem Soleimani and Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis.
US listed al-Muhandis.
A rat lines map of Iranian networks from Baghdad to Basra was leaked to Bill Roggio; the US surge and Iraqi forces targeted Shia groups until about 2010.
Al-Qaeda infographics claimed 340+ operations in Afghanistan in March, killing 500+ Afghan forces and overrunning 11 checkpoints.
US raid on two al-Qaeda camps in Shorabak, Kandahar; one was described as al-Qaeda's largest since 9/11, with 150-200 fighters killed.
US drone strike killed Hakimullah Mehsud.
Attempted Times Square bombing, claimed by the TTP; Hakimullah's media team sent Roggio a video claim.
Tahir Yuldashev was killed.
TTP released a video tribute to Hakimullah Mehsud showing Sirajuddin Haqqani, Sangeen Zadran and Tahir Yuldashev; released the same day as episode 5 of the podcast.
Khalilzad and Gen. Miller met the Pakistani military establishment in Islamabad; the US embassy praised Pakistan's peace efforts.
Asim Umar killed in Helmand, where the Mullah Dadullah Front had sheltered him.
Four Tajik suspects allegedly joined ISIS; their ringleader was imprisoned in March 2019.
German authorities announced they broke up a plot by four alleged Tajik ISIS members to attack US military facilities in Germany.
Five young Tajik men rammed and stabbed foreign cyclists in Tajikistan, killing four including two Americans; ISIS released a video via Amaq.
UN Monitoring Team report on ISKP recruiting Tajiks and naming Farooqi as replacement for Abu Omar al-Khorasani.
ISIS attacked a memorial service for Abdul Ali Mazari in Kabul; dozens killed or wounded.
Attack on a Sikh temple in Kabul killed more than two dozen civilians; ISIS claimed revenge for Kashmir; Afghan forces blame Farooqi.
Afghan forces detained Aslam Farooqi, alleged ISKP emir.
German authorities cracked down on an alleged ISIS-linked cell of Tajik citizens who were in contact with ISIS leaders in Syria and Afghanistan.

German authorities say a cell of Tajik citizens was in contact with ISIS leaders in both Syria and Afghanistan.
Indian Mujahideen was a front for Lashkar-e-Taiba, and its attackers were Indian citizens.
